sentences.text: Turicibacter sanguinis, described as a new species in a new genus, was isolated as a strictly anaerobic, Gram-positive rod from a blood culture of a febrile patient with acute appendicitis.
A study describes bacteria of the genus Turicibacter as prominent members of the mammalian gut microbiota that correlate with alterations in dietary fat and body weight.

That study characterised mouse- and human-derived Turicibacter isolates, found they group into clades differing in their transformations of specific bile acids, and identified bile salt hydrolases conferring strain-specific differences in bile deconjugation.

A study of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis reported that Turicibacter sanguinis was consistently enriched in all its models and public data sets, with abundance correlating positively with liver injury markers.
A study of gut microbiota composition in Lebanese subjects with autism spectrum disorders reported a lower abundance of Turicibacter in the autism and sibling groups than in controls.
